unit: A theme is counted once per interview, never per mention; themes overlap.

themes.theme: Offer disappears before the responder can answer
themes.impact: A willing response can be lost before it becomes an assignment; investigate timing separately from allocation.

evidence.aunt-dot: by the time he's actually got a thumb on the screen — it's gone.
evidence.ambrose: the young master was halfway into the suit — coat on, one boot on — when it went to somebody else.
evidence.halloran: Bulwark mentioned a callout went to someone else before he'd even got his boots on

themes.theme: Quiet stretches or unexplained differences in work
themes.impact: Customers cannot tell whether Dispatch still considers them for work; aggregate acceptance may hide lost access.

evidence.aunt-dot: there have been stretches, more than one, where the phone just sits there and sits there
evidence.kip: Mite thinks Mite's been forgotten. Gale's exhausted.

themes.theme: Text or status badges are hard to read at a glance
themes.impact: Handlers lose awareness while working at normal viewing distances.

evidence.aunt-dot: the text is small enough that from a normal standing distance I sometimes can't tell if something's changed unless I lean right in
evidence.ambrose: Larger text on the status badge.

themes.theme: Handler alerts are missing, easy to miss or hard to distinguish
themes.impact: The person coordinating readiness cannot reliably identify a live offer or which responder needs attention.

evidence.aunt-dot: maybe something that tells me too, not just him, when something's come in
evidence.ambrose: I would want whatever tells me a callout is live to be harder to miss, not easier.
evidence.kip: I want the alert sound to be different for each of them

themes.impact: The handler monitors an unintended view and loses trust in persistence.

evidence.ambrose: Twice now it's reverted to the default view

themes.theme: Capability-tag definitions are hard to reach
themes.impact: Intermittent lookup interrupts the handler's work; the participant calls this non-urgent.

evidence.ambrose: The capability tag legend. It sits in a drawer off the responder detail panel

themes.theme: Console brightness makes night work uncomfortable
themes.impact: Repeated exposure affects the whole shift; the workaround degrades other screens.

evidence.kip: I just want an actual dark theme built in.

themes.impact: A responder can remain in the field with damaged protective equipment while approval waits.

evidence.halloran: it sat waiting on a quartermaster signature for eleven days.

themes.theme: Urgent equipment requests share an ineffective priority queue
themes.impact: Protective-equipment replacement competes with routine items despite an urgency flag.

evidence.halloran: One queue, everything in it, doesn't matter if it's laces or plate.

themes.theme: Field-failure reports have no visible follow-up
themes.impact: Handlers cannot see whether reporting changes maintenance or equipment decisions.

evidence.halloran: I file a failure report and it goes into a void.

themes.theme: Equipment catalog search returns broad or irrelevant results
themes.impact: Handlers spend time finding suitable equipment and ask for category filters.

evidence.halloran: I typed "plate" the other week looking for the vest plate and got forty results, half of them unrelated
